title: Алматы лидирует по смертности от гриппа и ОРЗ, но и север не отстает
content: Almaty leads Kazakhstan in deaths from influenza, acute respiratory viral infections (ARVI), and pneumonia, with 241 fatalities—more than any other region. The highest regional death tolls followed in Kostanay and Karaganda regions (189 each), North Kazakhstan (139), and Akmola (121). These regions also had the highest proportions of deaths from these diseases relative to total mortality: 4.8% in Kostanay, 4.6% in North Kazakhstan, 4.0% in Almaty, and 3.6% in both Akmola and Karaganda. In contrast, Turkistan Region reported the lowest numbers: 14 deaths and a 0.4% share of total mortality. The source notes that while the low figures in Turkistan are expected due to its warmer southern climate, they may also reflect insufficient accuracy in recording actual causes of death, potentially affecting statistical reliability.

title: Усиление комплексного эпидемиологического надзора за гриппом и острыми респираторными инфекциями в Туркменистане - News Central Asia (nCa)
content: From October 7 to 11, 2025, the WHO Country Office in Turkmenistan conducted a technical mission aimed at strengthening the integrated epidemiological surveillance system for influenza and acute respiratory infections (ARI) in the country, as part of the Pandemic Influenza Preparedness Mechanism. The mission team included Dr. James Edward Fielding, WHO technical expert on respiratory virus surveillance, and WHO experts Kirill Stolyarov and Darya Danilenko. Experts provided advisory and technical support to national partners on implementing integrated sentinel surveillance for influenza and ARI, assessed the implementation of the updated surveillance protocol in expanded sentinel centers—including epidemiological and virological monitoring and data collection and analysis systems—and reviewed the electronic surveillance program, which was updated in line with revised national guidelines for routine and sentinel surveillance. A training seminar was held to build national capacity in principles of sentinel surveillance, mosaic surveillance, data management for influenza and ARI, and virological surveillance. WHO experts also participated in the scientific conference 'Healthcare, Education, and Sports in the Era of the Renaissance of a Powerful State,' held in honor of Turkmenistan’s Medical Worker Day. The mission included visits to key healthcare institutions in Ashgabat, such as Health House No. 10, the Directorate of Centers for Prevention of Infectious Diseases, the Sanitary-Epidemiological Service of Ashgabat, the State Sanitary-Epidemiological Service under the Ministry of Health and Medical Industry of Turkmenistan, and the Virology Reference Laboratory at the Center for Public Health and Nutrition. These visits included evaluations of virological surveillance for influenza and ARI and assessments of the operational capacity of the sentinel surveillance system. The mission concluded with a strategic discussion on findings, technical recommendations, and next steps to strengthen Turkmenistan’s integrated influenza and ARI surveillance system. WHO reaffirmed its commitment to continued collaboration in supporting Turkmenistan’s efforts to enhance preparedness and response in public health.

title: Обнародовано число смертей за последние 7 месяцев в Азербайджане
content: The State Statistics Committee of Azerbaijan reported that 34,994 deaths were registered in the country during the first seven months of 2025. The death rate per 1,000 residents remained unchanged at 5.9 compared with the same period in 2024, according to the agency. The report states, 'По сравнению с аналогичным периодом 2024 года показатель на каждые 1000 человек населения остался неизменным -- на уровне 5,9'.

title: Регионы с самой высокой смертностью в ДТП назвали в МВД РФ
content: The Russian Interior Ministry (MVD) released statistics on road‑traffic fatalities for 2024, highlighting the regions with the highest death tolls. In the Krasnodar Krai, 789 people died in accidents; the Moscow region saw 649 deaths, with 346 in Moscow city itself; and the Rostov region recorded 500 fatalities. Across the Central Federal District, the total exceeded 3.3 thousand deaths, while the Volga District had 2.9 thousand, the Ural District more than 1.1 thousand, and both the North‑West and North‑Caucasian Districts had over 1 thousand each. Nationwide, the MVD reported more than 14.4 thousand deaths in 2024. The ministry aims to reduce road‑traffic mortality by 50 % by 2030 and by 100 % by 2036, as outlined in the July 2025 “Strategy for Improving Road‑Traffic Safety.”

title: Названо число казахстанцев погибших от ЧС в 2025 году
content: According to the Ministry of Emergency Situations, there have been 8,500 emergency situations and natural disasters in Kazakhstan in the first seven months of 2025, a 29% increase from the same period last year. However, the number of fatalities has decreased by 15%, from 393 to 332 people. The main cause of emergencies is technological incidents, accounting for 90% of cases. The number of fires has increased by 25% to 6,800, but the material damage has decreased by 86% to 3.3 billion tenge. The most common causes of fires are faulty electrical wiring, improper use of fire, and equipment malfunctions. The number of fires in residential areas and transportation has increased significantly, with the highest growth rates seen in Pavlodar, Shymkent, Karaganda, Abai, and Almaty regions. Natural disasters accounted for 10% of the total number of emergencies, with 832 cases, a 33% increase from last year. The number of natural disasters has decreased by 27%.

title: В Казахстане зафиксирован рост числа пожаров
content: In 2025, Kazakhstan recorded a sharp rise in emergency incidents (ЧС) and fires. Over the first eight months, 9.7 thousand incidents were logged, a 25 % increase over 2024. The total number of injured people grew by 8.2 % to 1.3 thousand, while deaths fell 15.5 % to 144, yet the overall trend of rising incidents remains concerning. Ninety‑nine percent of incidents were of a technological nature, with 90 % of those being production‑house fires, indicating weak safety controls in industrial and residential settings. The Ministry of Emergency Situations (МЧС) carried out 21.7 thousand fire‑safety inspections, uncovering more than 104 thousand violations and holding 13.2 thousand individuals to administrative responsibility. In industrial safety, 492 preventive controls and 191 unscheduled checks identified 16 762 violations, leading to the suspension of 1 023 facilities. Fires themselves increased by 21.6 % to 7.8 thousand, yet material damage dropped 81.8 % from 21.5 million to 3.93 billion tenge. Natural emergencies accounted for 10.5 % of all incidents, with 1 021 cases (29.4 % higher than 2024), 564 injuries, and 144 fatalities; 52.9 % of natural emergencies were fires. The unified dispatch service received over 3.6 million calls, and МЧС rescued 9.1 thousand people, evacuated 9.6 thousand, and provided first aid to 3.1 thousand. These figures suggest that despite increased inspections, the growth in incidents and violations points to ineffective enforcement and insufficient safety measures, especially in the Pavlodar region where the rise is most pronounced.

title: Более 1 600 жертв: Казахстан оказался на третьем месте в мире по смертности в ДТП
content: According to the Procuracy of North Kazakhstan Region, Kazakhstan ranks third globally in traffic fatality rates, behind only Russia and the United States, based on data from the United Nations Economic Commission for Europe. The report, released on October 10, 2025, states that over 1,600 people died and more than 35,000 were injured in road accidents across Kazakhstan in the first nine months of 2025. The Procuracy attributes 86% of accidents to driver error, while 14% are due to pedestrians and other road users. The nationwide 'Safe Road' campaign, aimed at improving road safety and reducing accidents, was recently intensified. Earlier in February, the Senate discussed a nearly 100% increase in traffic accidents in 2024 compared to the previous year—over 30,000 incidents resulted in 40,000 injuries and more than 2,500 fatalities. The Genprocuracy had previously published regional statistics on fatal traffic accidents during the summer.

title: Euskadi registró 6.300 fallecimiento en el primer trimestre del año,...
content: Euskadi recorded 6,300 deaths in the first quarter of 2025, a 1 % increase over the same period in 2024, and a negative vegetative growth of 3,039 people, according to Eustat data. Monthly figures show a 2.1 % decline in January, an 8.3 % rise in February, and a 2 % drop in March. By historical territory, Álava had 854 deaths, up 6.1 %; Bizkaia 3,454 deaths, up 1.5 %; Gipuzkoa 1,992 deaths, down 2 %. Women accounted for 3,305 deaths (2.3 % rise) and men 2,995 deaths (0.4 % decline). Children under one year represented 0.1 % (5 deaths) and centenarians 2 % (128 deaths). The leading causes were circulatory system diseases (1,560 deaths) and tumors (1,529 deaths), together 49.1 % of all deaths. Respiratory system diseases caused 847 deaths (13.4 %), nervous system diseases 374 deaths (5.9 %), and digestive system diseases 301 deaths (4.8 %). Among men tumors surpassed circulatory diseases, while among women circulatory diseases were the top cause. Suicide or self‑inflicted injuries accounted for 171 deaths, 21.3 % higher than in 2023.
